findings: Actual C admission consists solely of native thread-local pointer load/store. Both C and C++ interfaces borrow the supplied context and restore the exact previous pointer; no JS/runtime value entitlement or VM call is introduced.

Each Fixture restores admission before context/runtime retirement. Explicit second-runtime destruction occurs only after its nested admission has restored the first context. Same-context and explicit-null nesting retain the actual caller pointer.

pi_js_new_runtime passes the real pi allocator to JS_NewRuntime2; its native owner limit32MiB is independent from the original VM malloc_limit0. The v2 control restores the saved actual before.malloc_limit with an explicit integer cast, after both native memory and VM memory observations under limit1.

Ordinary and actually flagged fatal pending values are independently retained, taken only after the admission observations and compared by real identity/flag. The private test observes actual published event plus stable generation before taking its token.

V2 installs cleanup immediately after taking the private reason. On every exit, an actual private token is republished through JS_Throw(DupValue), then Cancel sees its required actual pending condition, then the held reason retires. This closes the detached-lease cleanup finding without altering any preceding observation.

The C++ support constructs the admission Scope before its later ObserveRetirement object. Actual reverse local destruction gives both inner/outer destructor observations while the respective context is current. Normal mask63 includes post-inner bit16; early-return mask47 omits that bit and still observes both destructors and final caller restoration.

The worker creates and retires its own real VM on its actual thread, begins/ends with native TLS null, and is joined before the parent reads its flags or retires any shared native record. Thread-spawn failure still restores the parent's outer scope through its existing defers.
All raw reasons have cleanup before fallible identity assertions; native Probe/output records remain live through their actual C++ calls and thread join.
